a-2013-vision-saw-india-needing-746.text:
- Claim in post: "puts India's actual natural gas consumption at roughly 188 MMSCMD in FY2023-24 and roughly 197.1 MMSCMD in 2025"
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): An NSE-hosted "Performance review for FY25-26 – Natural Gas" (June 2026) gives consumption from the PPAC balance sheet: 68,542 MMSCM in FY2025-26 against 71,314 MMSCM in FY2024-25. That is about 188 MMSCMD for FY2025-26 against about 195 MMSCMD the year before (my own division by 365, not a published figure). Business Standard reported falling consumption in 2025 because of a long monsoon and cheaper alternative fuels. One conflicting figure exists: Polymerupdate/CARE gives 212 MMSCMD for FY2025-26. The newer full-year figure is lower, which strengthens the post's point. Seen: summaries only.
  - https://nsearchives.nseindia.com//web/mediaattachment/2026-06/Performance_review_for_FY25-26_-_Natural_Gas_20260630172900.pdf
  - https://www.business-standard.com/industry/news/gas-consumption-plummets-7-5-per-cent-amid-prolonged-monsoons-lower-alternate-fuel-prices-125121001165_1.html
  - https://www.polymerupdate.com/News/Details/1298408/important
- Suggested wording: "Update, October 2026: A PPAC-based industry summary puts FY2025-26 natural gas consumption at 68,542 MMSCM, about 188 MMSCMD, down from about 195 MMSCMD in FY2024-25. That is roughly a quarter of the 2013 report's 625.92 MMSCMD projection for 2025-26."
- Confidence: Single PPAC-derived source, seen as a summary. One conflicting estimate (212 MMSCMD) remains. The MMSCMD conversion is my own arithmetic.

annadata-to-urjadata-farmer-income-case.text:
- Claim in post: "FCI rice goes into ethanol at ₹2,320/quintal (₹60.32/litre)"; also, in the safeguards table, "Allocation valid only to 30 Jun 2026"; and "India's central-pool rice stock stood at ~377 lakh MT on 1 July 2025 and ~386 lakh MT in April 2026"
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): Summaries of Bioenergy Times and Outlook reporting say:
  - The government has set aside 7.2 million tonnes (72 lakh t) of FCI rice for ethanol for the 2026-27 supply year, up from 5.5 million tonnes the year before. The year-before figure differs from the post's 52 lakh MT, and the post places the 72 lakh MT raise within 2025-26.
  - The FCI rice issue price for ethanol is ₹2,320/quintal until 31 October 2026 and rises to ₹2,390/quintal from 1 November 2026, reported as covering November 2026 to June 2027.
  - Central-pool rice stocks were 403.11 lakh tonnes on 1 July 2026, nearly three times the buffer norm.
  - A Rajya Sabha reply put FCI's acquisition cost at ₹3,889.46/quintal for 2025-26 (revised estimate).

  Seen: summaries only.
  - https://bioenergytimes.com/higher-fci-rice-allocation-for-ethanol-to-support-e20-target-ease-grain-stockpile/
  - https://www.outlookindia.com/national/fci-sold-rice-to-ethanol-distilleries-at-nearly-40-below-acquisition-cost
- Suggested wording: "Updated 18 October 2026. Trade reports say the government has allocated about 72 lakh tonnes of FCI rice for ethanol in the 2026-27 supply year and that the FCI issue price rises from ₹2,320 to ₹2,390 a quintal from 1 November 2026. Central-pool rice stocks were reported at about 403 lakh tonnes on 1 July 2026. The OMC ethanol procurement prices for 2026-27 had not been found at the time of this note."
- Confidence: Two outlets agree on the price step-up. The allocation figures (5.5 vs 5.2 million tonnes for the prior year, and which year the 72 lakh t applies to) conflict with the post and between summaries, so check the FCI/DFPD order. No ESY 2026-27 OMC tender price was found.

effective-buying-power-china-comparison.text:
- Claim in post: "But India's implied inflation this year (~0.9%, from the FY2025-26 First Advance Estimate) was actually lower than the US's (~2.6–2.8%)". The caveats add: "FY2025-26 uses only a First Advance Estimate (7% real, 8% nominal) that will itself be revised."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **Provisional Estimates superseded the Advance Estimate before this post (2 Aug 2026).** MoSPI released FY2025-26 Provisional Estimates on 5 June 2026, on the new 2022-23 base series:
    - real GDP growth: 7.7%
    - nominal GDP growth: 8.9% (₹346.36 lakh crore against ₹318.07 lakh crore)
  - **The implied deflator is about 1.1%.** By this reviewer's arithmetic, 1.089 / 1.077 − 1 ≈ 1.1%, against the ~0.9% in the post. That is still well below US CPI, so the conclusion survives.
  - **The base series changed.** The earlier years in the chart are presumably on the old series, so the chain now mixes bases.
  - **The 7% real figure may not match.** One summary gives the earlier advance estimate as 7.4% real and 8.0% nominal, not the post's "7% real".
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.dailypioneer.com/news/india--039-s-gdp-grows-7-7--in-fy-2025-26--q4-growth-estimated-at-7-8-
  - https://newsonair.gov.in/indias-real-gdp-grows-by-7-7-in-2025-26/
  - https://www.manoramayearbook.in/current-affairs/india/2026/06/06/india-records-gdp-growth-in-fy25.html
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. MoSPI's Provisional Estimates for 2025-26 (5 June 2026, new 2022-23 base) put real GDP growth at 7.7% and nominal at 8.9%. That implies a GDP deflator of roughly 1.1%, not the ~0.9% used below from the Advance Estimate. India's implied inflation still ran below US CPI, so the conclusion that the past year's depreciation was essentially all real is unchanged. The real-rate series has not been recomputed."
- Confidence: several summaries agree on 7.7% and 8.9%, and one is from newsonair, the public broadcaster. The deflator is this reviewer's arithmetic. The effect of mixing base series on the chained index is unverified.

- Claim in post: "India's RBI is currently doing the opposite — selling reserves to stop the rupee falling further". It cites reserves that "fell from a $728.5bn peak to a $666.9bn trough, an 8.5% drawdown, precisely while the rupee was depreciating."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **Reserves set a new record, then fell again.** Business Today (8 Oct 2026, citing Bloomberg) reported:
    - a record $785bn in the week ended 4 September 2026
    - four straight weekly falls since, to $734bn in the week ended 2 October
  - **The post's main claim still holds.** The RBI was again selling dollars in the spot market and using sell/buy swaps.
  - **The rupee is near its record low.** It traded around ₹96.68–97, about 0.2% from the record low of ₹96.97 set in May 2026. The post's figure is ₹96.37 (17 Jul 2026).
  - **Unexplained:** what drove reserves from the $666.9bn trough to $785bn. It could be RBI purchases, which would bear on the "opposite of China" argument, or valuation gains.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/economy/story/rupee-near-record-low-why-rbis-multiple-defences-are-losing-effectiveness-560381-2026-10-08
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. The reserve peak and trough cited below have been overtaken. Per Business Today (8 October 2026, citing Bloomberg), reserves hit a record of about $785bn in early September 2026 and then fell for four straight weeks to about $734bn, with the RBI again selling dollars to defend a rupee near ₹97. The defensive direction of intervention described here still holds. This piece has not checked what drove the rise to the September record."
- Confidence: single secondary source. The cause of the reserve rebuild is unverified.

five-year-synthesis-trade-currency.text:
- Claim in post: "The path also turned: reserves peaked at $728.5bn on 27 Feb 2026, then fell to a $666.9bn trough on 26 Jun 2026 — an 8.5% peak-to-trough drawdown — so the final year of this window subtracted from reserves rather than adding to them." Same paragraph: "so import-cover in months has quietly thinned."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The drawdown has fully reversed.** RBI data reported on 9 October 2026 (PTI, carried by several outlets) put reserves at $734.61bn in the week ended 2 October 2026. That was after a weekly fall of $12.95bn, implying about $747.6bn a week earlier (reviewer's arithmetic). Both figures are above the post's $728.5bn "peak".
  - The same reports say reserves were about $43.5bn above their end-March 2026 level and about $34.6bn higher than a year earlier.
  - The existing 12 Oct 2026 note updates services, GDP and the rupee but not reserves.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://timesofoman.com/article/177845-indias-forex-reserves-fall-by-1295-billion-to-73461-billion-in-week-ended-oct-2
  - https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/business/3989801-indias-forex-reserves-fall-by-1295-billion-to-73461-billion-in-week-ended-oct-2-rbi
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. The reserves drawdown described here has since reversed. Per RBI weekly data as reported, reserves stood at $734.6 billion in the week ended 2 October 2026, above the February 2026 peak cited below and about $43.5 billion higher than at end-March 2026. The five-year comparison with import growth is unchanged."
- Confidence: several outlets carry the same PTI/RBI figure, so this is one underlying source. The RBI Weekly Statistical Supplement was not opened. The implied ~$747.6bn prior-week level is arithmetic, not a reported figure. The post's "import-cover thinned" point is about the five-year window and survives.

fy2025-26-sample-report-india-trade.text:
- Claim in post: "Use 675,157.0 (US$M), not 698,100.0, as "current" reserves — the two numbers are 13 months apart, not a contradiction." The reserves table labels 675,157.0 (as of 2026-07-10) "current, use this one". It lists "Forex reserves, all-time peak" at 728,494.0 on 2026-02-27, labelled "confirmed peak". It gives the USD/INR spot rate as 96.3665 on 2026-07-17, labelled "current".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **Reserves are now much higher.** ANI-syndicated reports (Times of Oman, Devdiscourse, NewKerala, 9–10 October 2026) say reserves fell $12.95 billion to $734.61 billion in the week ended 2 October 2026. They put that level $43.5 billion above end-March 2026.
  - **The "confirmed peak" has probably been passed.** Even after that fall, $734.61 billion is above the post's $728.49 billion peak. Adding the fall back gives about $747.6 billion for the week ended 25 September (this reviewer's arithmetic). If that is right, the February 2026 figure is no longer the all-time high.
  - **The rupee is also stale.** The latest spot rate found was 95.46 on 25 August 2026 (PTI via HDFC Sky). No October 2026 rate was found.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://timesofoman.com/article/177845-indias-forex-reserves-fall-by-1295-billion-to-73461-billion-in-week-ended-oct-2
  - https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/business/3989801-indias-forex-reserves-fall-by-1295-billion-to-73461-billion-in-week-ended-oct-2-rbi
  - https://hdfcsky.com/news/rupee-rises-24-paise-to-close-at-95-46-against-us-dollar
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. The reserves and exchange-rate rows below were current when this snapshot was compiled on 18 July 2026. Per RBI data reported by ANI, reserves stood at $734.61 billion in the week ended 2 October 2026, above the February 2026 figure labelled here as the all-time peak. The 'current' labels below should be read as 'as of July 2026'."
- Confidence: One wire story, syndicated by several outlets. The implied new peak is this reviewer's arithmetic and unverified. Check the RBI Weekly Statistical Supplement for the peak week and value before posting.

- Claim in post: "Services trade for FY2025-26 is not yet published — this repo's services/overall-balance figures run only through FY2024-25 (published one year behind goods trade), so no FY2025-26 services surplus or true "overall balance" figure exists yet."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **RBI has published full-year FY2025-26 balance-of-payments data.** Per search summaries:
    - current-account deficit of $25.2 billion (0.6% of GDP), against $22.9 billion in FY2024-25
    - a Q4 FY26 current-account surplus of $7.1 billion
    - Q4 net services receipts of $60.4 billion, up from $53.3 billion (Outlook Business)
  - **A full-year services surplus figure exists, from a secondary source.** An HDFC Mutual Fund note gives $216.6 billion for FY26. It was unclear whether that is net.
  - **Q1 FY2026-27 is also out.** Per Free Press Journal and ETV Bharat (around 1 September 2026): current-account deficit $4.2 billion (0.5% of GDP), net services receipts $51.6 billion.
  - The release date of the Q4 FY26 data was not confirmed in the summaries. It is usually late June, which would be before this report's 18 July compile date.
  - The post itself cites NITI Aayog's services-export growth of +9.0% for FY26.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.outlookbusiness.com/amp/story/news/india-records-71-bn-current-account-surplus-in-q4-fy26-rbi-data
  - https://www.hdfcfund.com/learn/deep-dives/tuesday-talking-point/underlying-resilience-indias-current-account-despite-challenging-macro-backdrop
  - https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/indias-current-account-deficit-widens-to-usd-42-billion-in-q1-fy27-rbi-data
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. RBI's balance-of-payments data now cover all of FY2025-26: per press reports, a current-account deficit of $25.2 billion (0.6% of GDP), with a Q4 surplus of $7.1 billion. An FY2025-26 overall-balance figure therefore exists, even though this repo's services series still stops at FY2024-25."
- Confidence: Two summaries agree on the RBI figures. The $216.6 billion services surplus comes from a single secondary source and is unverified. The publication date relative to 18 July is unverified.

india-ended-63-years-of-state-nuclear.text:
- Claim in post: "select fuel-cycle activities, including conversion, refining and enrichment of uranium-235, are now open to private entities up to a threshold value the government has yet to set, though the Act keeps unspecified "activities of a sensitive nature" under exclusive government control." The fixes section asks DAE to notify that threshold and publish the list of sensitive activities.
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The draft rules partly answer this.** The draft SHANTI Rules, 2026 (14 August 2026, comments to 4 September 2026) provide one composite licence to build, own, operate and decommission a plant. Private firms and joint ventures could also do nuclear R&D and manufacture nuclear fuel.
  - **Enrichment may not be open to private firms after all.** One summary says the draft keeps uranium and thorium enrichment or isotopic separation, and spent-fuel management, with the government. That would cut against the post's line that enrichment is open up to a threshold.
  - No threshold figure was found in the summaries. Whether the rules have been finalised since the comment period closed: unverified.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://visionias.in/current-affairs/news-today/2026-08-18/science-and-technology/draft-shanti-rules-2026-released-by-the-government
  - https://www.civilsdaily.com/news/draft-rules-under-the-shanti-act-open-nuclear-power-to-captive-industrial-use-and-a-composite-licence/
  - https://www.shankariasparliament.com/current-affairs/draft-shanti-rules-2026
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. DAE published draft SHANTI Rules on 14 August 2026, with comments invited until 4 September. Summaries describe a single composite licence for private and joint-venture operators. They also say enrichment, isotopic separation and spent-fuel management stay with the government, so the fuel-cycle opening described below may be narrower in practice. We have not seen the final rules."
- Confidence: Several exam-prep summaries agree on the release date and the composite licence. The reserved-activities list comes from a single summary and is unverified. The question is whether enrichment is reserved in the rules even though the Act allows it.

indian-railways-98-to-earn-100-business.text:
- Claim in post: "Indian Railways is budgeted to spend ₹98.43 to earn every ₹100 in FY2025-26 — an operating ratio that has stayed above 96% every year since 2016-17." The post also says: "Railways budgeted ₹2,65,200 crore in capital expenditure for FY2025-26".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The 98.43% budget target was missed.** Union Budget 2026-27 (1 Feb 2026) revised the FY2025-26 operating ratio to 98.82%, worse than the post's 98.43% budget estimate. FY2026-27 is budgeted at 98.4%.
  - **Capex:** FY2026-27 railway capex was set at a record ₹2.92 lakh crore.
  - **PRS has a newer analysis.** Its Demand for Grants 2026-27 analysis says the ratio stays above 98% and puts FY27 internal revenue at ₹3.02 lakh crore. The post cites PRS's February 2025 analysis.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.business-standard.com/budget/news/indian-railways-record-capex-fy27-high-speed-rail-freight-corridor-126020100735_1.html
  - https://indianinfrastructure.com/2026/02/05/indian-railways-estimates-passenger-revenue-of-rs-873-billion-during-fy-2026-27/
  - https://prsindia.org/budgets/parliament/demand-for-grants-2026-27-analysis-railways
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. This piece uses the FY2025-26 budget estimates. Per press coverage of the 2026-27 Budget, the FY2025-26 operating ratio was revised to 98.82%, worse than the 98.43% budgeted. FY2026-27 is budgeted at 98.4%, with record capital spending of about ₹2.92 lakh crore. The near-100% pattern described here continues."
- Confidence: Business Standard and Indian Infrastructure agree on 98.82% and 98.4%, and PRS's summary agrees with "above 98%". FY2025-26 actuals are not yet available.

indias-epr-regime-just-got-teeth-and.text:
- Claim in post: "Whether the ₹1,500 crore NCMM recycling incentive has been disbursed or remains an approved-but-unspent allocation — not established here."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): The scheme was notified on 2 October 2025 and its application window ran to 1 April 2026. The Ministry of Mines' Executive Committee approved 20 entities on 30 March 2026 and 38 on 29 April 2026, 58 eligible firms in all. Together they pledged about 850 KTPA of capacity and about ₹5,000 crore of investment, covering battery recycling, e-waste and other streams. The summaries say support is linked to project-implementation progress, and no disbursed amount was found. This predates the post (8 August 2026). The post's point survives, since selection is not disbursement, but "approved allocation" understates where the scheme stands. Seen: summaries only.
  - https://newsonair.gov.in/ministry-of-mines-approves-58-companies-under-incentive-scheme-for-promotion-of-critical-mineral-recycling/
  - https://www.energetica-india.net/news/govt-approves-58-firms-under-critical-mineral-recycling-scheme
  - https://www.angelone.in/news/economy/india-selects-58-companies-under-critical-mineral-recycling-scheme-5-000-crore-investment-pledged
- Suggested wording: "Updated 18 October 2026. The Ministry of Mines had by April 2026 approved 58 companies as eligible under the ₹1,500 crore critical-mineral recycling incentive, pledging about ₹5,000 crore of investment, according to press reports. Payments are linked to project progress, and no disbursement figure was found for this note."
- Confidence: Three outlets agree on the 58 firms. They differ only on the report date (30 April to 5 May 2026).

indias-oil-fields-are-running-down-3696.text:
- Claim in post: "crude oil production has fallen from 36.96 MMT in 2015-16 to 28.70 MMT in 2024-25". It also says "Import dependency for crude is quoted at 88.2%, and that is the figure usually cited."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **FY2025-26 provisional figures exist.** ThePrint reports a Rajya Sabha written reply giving domestic crude production of 28.0 MMT and import dependence of 88.7% for 2025-26 (provisional), a record high.
  - **A third straight annual decline.** An OilPrice-based report describes FY2025-26 as the third straight annual decline, at about −3%. By this reviewer's arithmetic, 28.70 to 28.0 is about −2.4%, so the size of the fall differs between sources.
  - **Gas:** no national FY2025-26 gas figure was found. Oil India alone reported 3.450 MMT of crude and 3.186 BCM of gas for FY26.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://theprint.in/economy/indias-crude-import-dependence-rises-to-record-88-7-as-domestic-output-continues-to-decline/2998114/
  - https://newsable.asianetnews.com/business/oil-india-targets-4-mmt-crude-oil-production-this-year-says-cmd-articleshow-8lgftty
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. Since publication, a government reply to the Rajya Sabha (as reported) put 2025-26 crude production at about 28.0 MMT (provisional), down again from 28.70 MMT. Crude import dependence was put at a record 88.7%. The decline described here continued for a further year."
- Confidence: single secondary source for the 28.0 MMT and 88.7% figures, and both are provisional. The size of the fall differs across summaries. Confirm against PPAC's annual data before posting.

indias-trade-balance-hsn-wise.text:
- Claim in post: "Services data (RBI BoP) runs FY2015-16 to FY2024-25; goods data (TRADESTAT) runs FY2018-19 to FY2025-26". The post adds: "Even with services trade included, India ran a current-account-style deficit every year from FY2018-19 to FY2024-25". It also says "FY2025-26 is the most recent, not necessarily complete".

    - Current-account deficit: $25.2bn (0.6% of GDP), against $22.9bn in FY2024-25.
    - Q4 FY26 current-account surplus: $7.1bn.
    - Q4 net services receipts: $60.4bn, against $53.3bn a year earlier.
    - The full-year net-services total was not found in the summaries.

  - **The year is complete.** FY2025-26 has closed, though the data is still provisional, so "not necessarily complete" is out of date.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.outlookbusiness.com/news/india-records-71-bn-current-account-surplus-in-q4-fy26-rbi-data

RBI's full-year balance of payments, released in June 2026, shows a current-account deficit of about $25.2bn (0.6% of GDP). Commerce Ministry estimates put the combined goods-and-services deficit at about $119bn, wider than FY2024-25's $94.7bn. The services offset described here held in FY2025-26 but did not stop the combined gap from widening."

  - **The week before was about $747.6bn** by this reviewer's arithmetic.
  - **Comparisons:** reserves were $43.5bn above end-March 2026 and $34.6bn higher year on year.

- Confidence: two syndications of the same ANI report agree. The all-time peak date and value were not established. The search tool flagged that some other results showed mismatched dates, but not these two.

interest-subvention-built-499-ethanol.text:
- Claim in post: "Result: 499 distilleries operating in ESY 2024-25, national capacity at 1,822 crore litres/year, with 38 more distilleries in the pipeline adding a further 169 crore litres — capacity growth that outran the original 2030 target years early."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026): Higher capacity figures were in circulation before the post went up on 25/26 August 2026. Bioenergy Times (24 July 2026) reports about 1,990 crore litres, which the search summary attributes to November 2025 government data. IANS (15 May 2026) reports about 2,000 crore litres, exceeding demand. The search summary attributes a figure of 478 plants with 2,019 crore litres to a Rajya Sabha reply reported by Business Today (5 August 2026). The plant count (478) is lower than the post's 499, probably because of a different scope (plants versus distilleries, or a different date), so it should not be treated as a correction of the 499 figure. The post's point survives: 1G capacity far outran demand and the target. Seen: summaries only.
  - https://bioenergytimes.com/ethanol-production-capacity-rises-to-1990-crore-litres-in-india/
  - https://ianslive.in/indias-ethanol-capacity-at-2000-crore-litre-exceeds-demand-report--20260515152808
  - https://www.businesstoday.in/india/story/govt-approves-rs4687-crore-to-fuel-indias-ethanol-push-547493-2026-08-05
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]: Later government figures, as reported in the press, put India's ethanol capacity at roughly 1,990–2,019 crore litres a year (Bioenergy Times, July 2026; Business Today, August 2026, citing a Rajya Sabha reply). Plant counts in those reports use a different basis from the 499 figure below."
- Confidence: Medium on the roughly 2,000 crore litre level, since several outlets agree. Low on the exact 2,019 crore litre / 478 plant figures, which come from one summarised source. Also checked: HPCL Bathinda's "October 2026" target. The latest report found (Bioenergy Times, around July 2026) still says "by October" with about 97% of construction complete, and no commissioning was confirmed. The first, the Kakatiya Mega Textile Park at Warangal, was inaugurated on 10 May 2026 and is reported to have begun commercial production. securitising-deficit-what-it-would.text:

The facility stays open to 15 January 2027 for those flows. 30 September 2026 was the cut-off for the FCNR(B) leg, not the ECB leg. No extension beyond 31 December was found. The post's own FCNR(B) row in the same exhibit already says the facility "stays open for overseas borrowing (OFCBs/ECBs) to 31 December 2026", so the ECB row contradicts the post and gives a passed end date for a facility that is still open. The post's argument is unaffected. Seen: summaries only.

Under the RBI's 8 June 2026 circular, as summarised by law-firm and advisory notes, ECB and OFCB inflows qualify up to 31 December 2026 and the swap window stays open to 15 January 2027. The 30 September date applied only to the FCNR(B) leg, which the RBI closed early on 31 August."

No 2026 announcement of selected ports was found. Seen: summaries only.

upi-fees-are-now-legal-petrol-pumps.text:
- Claim in post: "The dealer’s commission is a fixed rupee amount per litre — ₹4.40 on petrol against a ₹94.77 Delhi pump price (4.6%), ₹3.03 on diesel against ₹87.67 (3.5%), per PPAC’s own price build-up." The stat strip shows "3.87%Blended dealer margin on the pump-price ticket" and "25.9×Leverage of a full-ticket fee on that margin". Exhibit 4 uses "Delhi prices of 01.10.2025 (petrol ₹94.77/L, diesel ₹87.67/L)".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **The pump prices were already out of date when the post was published.** Per the known since-events list, Delhi pump prices rose from 15 May 2026 to ₹102.12/l petrol and ₹95.20/l diesel. The post (8 Aug 2026) presents the 1 October 2025 prices in the present tense.
  - **The dealer commission appears unchanged, but that is unverified.** One search found no 2026 revision of Indian dealer commission; the results were about Pakistan.
  - **At the new prices, the margin is thinner and the leverage higher.** This is reviewer arithmetic on the post's own Exhibit 2 volumes, holding commission at ₹4.40/₹3.03:
    - ticket value: about ₹1.34 crore a month, against the ₹1.23 crore in Exhibit 2
    - blended margin: about 3.57%
    - leverage: about 28.0×
  - **Exhibit 4 tank values also rise.** At the new prices they are about ₹1,021, ₹4,085 and ₹28,560.
  - **The point survives.** A full-ticket fee hits the dealer harder at higher prices. The excise cut of 26 Mar 2026 does not affect dealer commission.
  - Seen: known since-events list; no page opened.
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. Delhi pump prices have been ₹102.12 (petrol) and ₹95.20 (diesel) a litre since 15 May 2026, above the 1 October 2025 build-up used below. If dealer commission is unchanged, the blended margin falls from 3.87% to about 3.57% of the ticket. The leverage of a full-ticket fee rises to about 28×, which strengthens this piece's exposure argument."
- Confidence: pump prices are from the established since-events list. That dealer commission is unchanged is unverified (one search, no Indian 2026 revision found).
